name: login_record_tampering
description: An intruder who edits the login history rather than deleting it. Truncating wtmp is the loud version and its file size gives it away; this removes ONE session and leaves the file full of plausible records, which is what a careful operator does and what `last` cannot report on. The only thing that can show it is a second database written independently by the same login: lastlog still holds the session wtmp no longer has. That is the entire reason the collection copies these files byte-for-byte instead of shipping `last` output, and until login_records.py existed nothing read them.

expect.id: raw wtmp is captured, not just `last` output
raw lastlog is captured — the independent record
the removed session is FLAGGED by cross-checking the two databases
the surviving sessions are still parsed and summarised
a file full of plausible records is NOT called a truncation
and it is not called a sequence break either — the kept records are in order
